question.knowledge_point: Finding the Range of a Transformed Function
question.problem: Find the range of the function $f(x)=2\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x+5).$
question.worked_solution:
The range of $\operatorname{csc}⁡x$ consists of two intervals:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡x\in (-\infty ,-1]\cup [1,\infty )
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x+5)\in (-\infty ,-1]\cup [1,\infty ).
$$

We can split this into two inequalities:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x+5)\le -1,\,\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x+5)\ge 1
$$

To find the range of $f(x),$ we consider both intervals separately.

- Multiplying the first interval by $2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{csc}⁡(4x+5)\le -1 \\  & 2\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x+5)\le -2 \\  & f(x)\le -2.\end{aligned}
$$

- Multiplying the second interval by $2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{csc}⁡(4x+5)\ge 1 \\  & 2\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x+5)\ge 2 \\  & f(x)\ge 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining both inequalities, we get

$$
f(x)\le -2,\,f(x)\ge 2.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the range is $f(x)\in (-\infty ,-2]\cup [2,\infty ).$
